# Thrush of Caregiver Hours (`thrush-of-caregiver-hours`)

Checks home care caregiver hours and pay: weekly hours across all clients with travel between clients counted, overtime owed against what payroll paid, split shifts and missed meal breaks under the state settings you give, and live-in sleep time that must be paid. Caregiver names are masked before results reach the model.

**Thrush never runs or changes payroll. Thrush never changes schedules or contacts caregivers.**

Kestrel ver 1 · Home care · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · patient and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`kestrel-core`](../kestrel-core)

```bash
npx -y thrush-of-caregiver-hours demo
npx -y thrush-of-caregiver-hours mcp --root ./practice-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional data only: a made-up home care agency, caregivers and clients. Any likeness to real people is chance. The settings are examples, not any state's law.

- [`shifts.csv`](fixtures/shifts.csv) and [`payroll.csv`](fixtures/payroll.csv) for the week of November 2, 2026. Planted:
  - Ana Ruiz: two clients a day with 20 minutes between them, Monday to Friday: 45 hours of shifts plus 1.67 hours of travel. Payroll paid 40 regular and 5 overtime, missing the travel.
  - Bo Chen: a 6.5-hour shift with no meal break (meal rule set at 5 hours).
  - Cy Ames: two shifts with a 4-hour unpaid gap (split shift).
  - Di Park: a 24-hour live-in shift with 10 hours of sleep recorded; only 8 may be left unpaid, so 2 count back as worked. Payroll paid 13 hours, short of the 15 worked.
- [`settings.json`](fixtures/settings.json): 40-hour week from Monday, 60-minute travel window, a 16.50 split premium, a meal break after 5 hours, an 8-hour sleep cap. [`settings-typo.json`](fixtures/settings-typo.json) misspells a setting and is refused.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `thrush_check` | List weeks paid short, missed meal breaks, live-in sleep to pay, split shifts, travel time and overtime weeks. | runs |
| `thrush_write_report` | Write thrush-caregiver-hours.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and thrush-caregiver-hours.html into out_dir (default kestrel-out/thrush). | runs |
| `thrush_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `thrush_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `thrush_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `thrush_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `payroll_submit` | Thrush never runs or changes payroll. | refused |
| `schedule_change` | Thrush never changes schedules or contacts caregivers. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `thrush_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `shifts` (required) | Shift or visit export under --root: caregiver, client, date, clock in and out (or minutes), meal minutes, live-in, sleep minutes and interruptions, pay rate |
| `payroll` | Optional payroll hours by week: caregiver, week start, regular hours, overtime hours |
| `settings` | Optional settings JSON: ot_hours, week_start, max_travel_minutes, split_gap_minutes, split_premium, meal_after_hours, meal_minutes, sleep_cap_minutes |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold patient or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx thrush-of-caregiver-hours inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Shifts (`shifts`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `caregiver_id` | text (masked) | Caregiver ID, Worker ID, Aide ID, Employee ID, Staff ID, Emp ID |
| `caregiver_name` | text (masked) | Caregiver, Caregiver Name, Worker, Aide, Employee, Employee Name, Staff Name |
| `client_id` | text (masked) | Client ID, Client, Client #, Member ID |
| `date` (required) | date | Date of Service, DOS, Service Date, Visit Date, Date, From DOS, Session Date, Appointment Date |
| `clock_in` | text | Clock In, Start, Time In, Shift Start |
| `clock_out` | text | Clock Out, End, Time Out, Shift End |
| `minutes` | number | Minutes, Min, Mins, Duration, Duration (min), Time (min), Total Minutes, Treatment Minutes |
| `meal_minutes` | number | Meal Minutes, Meal Break, Break Minutes, Lunch Minutes |
| `live_in` | text | Live In, Live-In, Live-in Shift, 24 Hour |
| `sleep_minutes` | number | Sleep Minutes, Sleep Time, Sleep |
| `sleep_interrupted` | text | Sleep Interrupted, Interrupted, Sleep Interruptions |
| `pay_rate` | amount | Pay Rate, Rate, Hourly Rate, Wage |

### Payroll hours (`payroll`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `caregiver_id` | text (masked) | Caregiver ID, Worker ID, Aide ID, Employee ID, Staff ID, Emp ID |
| `caregiver_name` | text (masked) | Caregiver, Caregiver Name, Worker, Aide, Employee, Employee Name, Staff Name |
| `week_start` (required) | date | Week Start, Week, Week Of, Period Start, Pay Week |
| `regular_hours` | number | Regular Hours, Reg Hours, Regular, REG |
| `overtime_hours` | number | Overtime Hours, OT Hours, Overtime, OT |

## Settings file (`thrush_settings`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `ot_hours` | Weekly hours after which overtime is owed; default 40 |
| `week_start` | First day of your workweek; default monday |
| `max_travel_minutes` | Same-day gaps between different clients up to this many minutes count as travel worked; default 60 |
| `split_gap_minutes` | Longer unpaid gaps count as a split shift; default 60 |
| `split_premium` | Split-shift premium your state requires, per split; off when not set |
| `meal_after_hours` | Shifts longer than this need a meal break under your state rules; off when not set |
| `meal_minutes` | Length of the required meal break; default 30 |
| `sleep_cap_minutes` | Most live-in sleep time that may be left unpaid; default 480 |

## Memory

`thrush_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `thrush_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `kestrel-core` and `remedy-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "thrush-of-caregiver-hours": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "thrush-of-caregiver-hours",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/practice-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add thrush-of-caregiver-hours -- npx -y thrush-of-caregiver-hours mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
thrush-of-caregiver-hours tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
thrush-of-caregiver-hours sources               # the columns each input is read from
thrush-of-caregiver-hours inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)

thrush-of-caregiver-hours eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
thrush-of-caregiver-hours demo
```

## Patient and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: patient and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to an EHR, practice-management system, payer portal, clearinghouse, state system, HR or payroll system, or bank.
- Payer, Medicare, Medicaid, state and federal rules are summarised from public material as of 2026, and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, compliance or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, billing, coding, tax, clinical or HIPAA advice. It does not diagnose or recommend care. A person decides what to bill, pay, report, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
